title: Local cohomological dimension bounds an isolated intersection
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local ring of finite dimension [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], $I\subsetneq A$ an ideal, and $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For a finitely generated ideal $K$ of a ring $A$, write $H_K^j(M)=R^j\Gamma_K(M)$, where $\Gamma_K(M)=\{x\in M:K^nx=0\text{ for some }n\}$, and let $\operatorname{cd}(A,K)$ be the least integer $q\geq-1$ such that $H_K^j(M)=0$ for every $A$-module $M$ and every $j>q$. If a closed subset $Z\subseteq X$ satisfies $Z\cap V(I)=\{\mathfrak m\}$, then $\dim Z\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)$. In particular, for a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ with $V(\mathfrak p)\cap V(I)=\{\mathfrak m\}$, one has $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)$.

source.place: Tag 0DXF (lemma-cd-bound-dim-local), including its closed-subset consequence obtained by applying it to the finitely many irreducible components; used in both dimension comparisons of Algebraization Tag 0ECR (lemma-punctured-still-connected).

proof.text: Write $Z=V(J)$ for an ideal $J\subseteq A$, as closed subsets of the Zariski spectrum have this form. The hypothesis implies $\mathfrak m\in Z$, so $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and $J\ne A$. Put $B=A/J$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m/J$. This is a nonzero Noetherian local ring: ideals of $B$ correspond to ideals of $A$ containing $J$ and are generated by the images of generators of their inverse images; a class outside $\mathfrak n$ has a representative outside $\mathfrak m$, hence is a unit. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is homeomorphic to $Z$. Thus $d=\dim\operatorname{Spec}B=\dim Z$; this dimension is finite, since every chain of irreducible closed subsets of the closed subspace $Z$ is such a chain in $X$. Here dimension is [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Tag 0DXF (lemma-cd-bound-dim-local), quotient reduction, applied to an ideal defining the whole closed subset.

proof.text: Put $L=IB\subseteq B$. Under the quotient-spectrum homeomorphism of Step 1, a prime of $B$ contains $L$ exactly when its inverse image contains both $J$ and $I$. The hypothesis therefore gives $V_B(L)=\{\mathfrak n\}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], specifically its formula for the radical as the intersection of the primes containing the ideal: $\sqrt L=\mathfrak n$. In particular $L\subseteq\mathfrak n$.

source.place: Tag 0DXF (lemma-cd-bound-dim-local), the support becomes the closed point after quotienting.

proof.text: By Noetherianity [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose generators $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ of $\mathfrak n$. Since $\sqrt L=\mathfrak n$, choose $e_i\geq1$ with $x_i^{e_i}\in L$. For $N=1+\sum_i(e_i-1)$ every degree-$N$ monomial in the generators contains some $x_i^{e_i}$, so $\mathfrak n^N\subseteq L\subseteq\mathfrak n$ (if $r=0$, both ideals are zero and take $N=1$). For every $B$-module $M$, $L^k x=0$ implies $\mathfrak n^{Nk}x=0$, and $\mathfrak n^k x=0$ implies $L^kx=0$. Hence $\Gamma_L(M)=\Gamma_{\mathfrak n}(M)$ naturally as submodules of $M$. Applying the identical functors to a single injective resolution gives identical right derived functors, and therefore $\operatorname{cd}(B,L)=\operatorname{cd}(B,\mathfrak n)$.

source.place: Tag 0DXF (lemma-cd-bound-dim-local), expanded justification of the equality of cohomological dimensions for the same support.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-local-cohomology-change-rings] to the quotient map $A\to B$: both rings are Noetherian by Step 1, and it gives $\operatorname{cd}(B,L)\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)$. Apply [lem-per-local-cohomology-top-nonvanishing] to the nonzero Noetherian local ring $(B,\mathfrak n)$ of finite dimension $d$: $H^d_{\mathfrak n}(B)\ne0$. By the defining vanishing property of $\operatorname{cd}(B,\mathfrak n)$ this forces $d\leq\operatorname{cd}(B,\mathfrak n)$. Using Step 3 and Step 1 yields $\dim Z=d\leq\operatorname{cd}(B,\mathfrak n)=\operatorname{cd}(B,L)\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)$.

source.place: Tag 0DXF (lemma-cd-bound-dim-local), first and last inequalities, using Tags 0DXA and 0DXE.

proof.text: For the particular case take $Z=V(\mathfrak p)$. It is closed and has the required intersection by assumption. The same quotient-spectrum homeomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] identifies it with $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p)$, so the bound just proved is $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)$.

Statement: the 0DXF prime case is kept verbatim as the 'in particular' clause. The closed-Z extension is true, via irreducible components, and is proved directly by applying the same quotient argument to B=A/J. 0DXE needs no domain hypothesis, so this works. Steps: (1) Z=V(J) with m in Z, so B=A/J is nonzero Noetherian local, and Spec B is homeomorphic to Z by the spec-quotient leaf. (2) V_B(IB)={n}, so sqrt(IB)=n by the radical leaf. (3) n^N is contained in IB by the pigeonhole bound on monomials, so Gamma_{IB}=Gamma_n and the two cd's are equal; this is truly elementary and r=0 is handled. (4) change-rings and top-nonvanishing give d <= cd(B,n) = cd(B,IB) <= cd(A,I). (5) The prime case follows. New nodes: change-rings is 0DXA restricted to Noetherian rings. It is true for derived torsion functors on modules, because Cech complexes agree under restriction of scalars. top-nonvanishing is the first half of 0DXE, checked on d=0 and on k[[x]].
